condition.title: Problem
condition.p: The browser takes a very long time to open a document.

cause.title: Cause
cause.p: Several factors can slow loading, including a slow network connection, a customization that interferes with document loading, or large documents.

steps-informal.p: In most cases, a customization (a plugin, framework, or custom option) causes slow loading. Try to reproduce the problem without customizations.
Update to the latest version and check whether the problem persists.

ol.li: Open a document that takes a long time to load in Web Author with Google Chrome.
Open the Developer Tools (e.g. by pressing F12).
Deselect the Disable cache checkbox in the Network tab.
Clear the requests.
Reload the page.
Right-click on a request and select Save all as HAR with content.
Sort the requests by time (e.g. right-click, Sort, Time).
Look for the longest requests. Inspect their URLs to determine whether a customization (a custom plugin or framework) generated them.
If you do not find a relevant request, send the downloaded HAR file to Oxygen Support.

steps-informal.p: Troubleshoot server requests by enabling verbose HTTP(S) logs:

ol.li: Enable verbose HTTP logs by following the procedure from Enabling HTTP Request Logging for Debugging.
Reproduce the problem.
Open the server logs by following the procedure from How to Locate the Log File and the Log Configuration File​.
Review the logs for requests that take a long time on the server.
If you do not find relevant information, send the logs to Oxygen Support.

steps-informal.p: Review the server logs for warnings:

ol.li: Open the server logs by following the procedure from How to Locate the Log File and the Log Configuration File.
Look for "Long request" and "Took long time to compute", then review the URLs of requests that take a long time on the server.
If nothing relevant is found, report the found logs to the Oxygen support team.

steps-informal.p: Sometimes documents load slowly because computing styles takes time. This time increases linearly with the size of the document and the CSS rules. The framework provides most CSS rules. Styles are computed on both the server and client.
To determine how long the browser takes to render the page:

ol.li: Open the Developer Tools in Google Chrome (e.g. by pressing F12).
Go to the Performance tab.
Click on Record in the top-left corner.
Reload the page.
When the page fully loads, click Stop.
Click the Main section within the Performance tab.
In the lower pane, open the Summary tab. A circle shows the load time divided among "Scripting", "Rendering", "Paint", "Idle", and "Other".
Check that "Rendering" time is reasonable.

steps-informal.p: Sometimes documents load slowly even if the main opened document is small, because it references many other documents that get expanded by either xi:include XML elements or DITA conref or conkeyref attributes.

For each referenced document that gets expanded, the application makes a request to an external server to retrieve the document content, thus the network speed and latency between the Web Author server and the server from where documents are retrieved is critical.

To troubleshoot this, enable network logs by following steps in Alternative Solution 3 and count how many requests are made when opening a document and how much time those requests took.
